question: Can a smaller factor base with random relations obtain the missing compact S-unit basis on the fixed 103b2 pair within the existing memory envelope?
inputs: Previously certified reduced cubic, maximal order and S_finite from the matched class-boundary certificate. No point coordinates or character masks are projected into the worker input.
method: PARI bnfinit with flag 1 and tech=[0.03,0.03,-1], then bnfunits on all prime ideals above S. Retain compact factorizations before attempting any certification. This changes relation strategy and factor-base size, not the tested fields or computational memory limit.
method_source: B. Allombert, PARI 2026 class groups tutorial, slides 2-3 and 9-10: https://pari.math.u-bordeaux.fr/Events/PARI2026/talks/bnfinit.pdf
positive_control: Run the same bnfinit/bnfunits interface on x^3-11 with S above 2,3,11 before either research field; verify its class group using bnfcertify.
failure_semantics: A timeout or stack exhaustion remains UNKNOWN class group and UNKNOWN S-unit basis. No rerun with more resources or changed parameters. A returned uncertified BNF is labelled conditional, not an exact class-group certificate.
boundary: Equation-only bounded retrospective computation. No new parameter or point search, no exceptional inputs, no active worker or candidate-policy changes.
